question.text: Under SEBI guidelines (April 10, 2023 circular) on excusing or excluding an investor from an AIF investment, which of the following is NOT a valid ground?

answer.text: Based on legal opinion, participation would violate applicable law or regulation for that investor
Investor has disclosed in Contribution Agreement that participation would contravene their internal policy
Manager is satisfied that participation would cause the AIF scheme to violate law or adversely affect it
Another investor in the same scheme has offered a side-letter paying 0.25% extra fee to exclude the investor

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Valid grounds for excusing/excluding: (i) legal-opinion-backed regulatory violation for the investor; (ii) investor's pre-disclosed internal-policy contravention; (iii) Manager satisfied participation would cause scheme-level violation or adverse impact; (iv) look-through excusal for investment-vehicle investors. Side-letter financial-incentive-based exclusion is NOT a ground and would also be a pari-passu violation. **The Trap:** Options A, B, C are straight from the circular. D invents an economic pay-off that violates pari-passu rights. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C/D test the excuse/exclude matrix. XIX-E frames around a Cat III long-short fund managing SEC-regulated US investor participation. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Document rationale + supporting evidence for every excusal. Reporting internal-policy change is 15 days from investor side — write this into your contribution agreement.
